description.text: Regal Rexnord Corporation (NYSE: RRX) (“we,” “us,” “our” or the “Company”) and its associates around the world help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company's automation offering, comprised of controllers, drives, precision motors, and actuators, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision tools used in surgical applications. The Company is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin and has manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. The Company is comprised of three operating segments: Automation & Motion Control ("AMC"), Industrial Powertrain Solutions ("IPS"), and Power Efficiency Solutions ("PES"). A description of the three operating segments is as follows: •The AMC segment designs, produces and services conveyor products, conveying automation subsystems, aerospace components, precision motion control solutions, high-efficiency miniature servo motors, controls, drives and linear actuators, as well as power management products that include automatic transfer switches, paralleling switchgear, and customized modular electric pod solutions ("E-Pods") that comprise relevant power and thermal management content.

about.description_short: Regal Rexnord's 30,000 associates around the world help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company's electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company's automation offering, comprised of controllers, drives, precision motors, and actuators, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision tools used in surgical applications. The Company's end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include discrete automation, food & beverage, aerospace & defense, medical, data center, energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, and metals and mining.

analysis_md:
# RRX — Regal Rexnord Corporation
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-18, engine 5.4.0. Price $154.01 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $10.257B — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Milwaukee industrial that powers, transmits and controls motion, built by deal-making: Regal Beloit merged with Rexnord's Process & Motion Control business in 2021, then acquired Altra Industrial Motion for ~$4.95B in March 2023, then sold the bulk of its Industrial Systems segment (industrial motors & generators) to WEG in 2024. Three segments remain (FY2025 revenue $5,934.5M total): Industrial Powertrain Solutions (IPS — gear drives, couplings, bearings, brakes, conveying; the largest), Automation & Motion Control (AMC — Kollmorgen/Portescap/Thomson precision motors, drives and linear motion from Altra), and Power Efficiency Solutions (PES — motors and air-moving for HVAC/pool). End markets: discrete automation, data centers (including its ePOD modular power ramp), aerospace & defense, food & beverage, mining, commercial/residential HVAC. Competitors: ABB, Siemens, Emerson, Rockwell, Timken, SKF, Gates. A new CEO, Aamir Paul, took over July 1, 2026.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $990,800,000; capex $97,700,000; SBC $37,300,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $855,800,000 = $12.85/share** — but see BASE_DIVERGENCE below: this year is flattered and is NOT the base.
- Maintenance version FY2025 (from financials_history.csv): $552,100,000 — far below the conservative figure, the gap being the FY2025 working-capital release (delta NWC −$215,800,000 in the history file).
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $4,267,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json; LongTermDebtNoncurrent+LongTermDebtCurrent basis), plus lease liabilities $152,500,000. Q2 2026 release put net debt at 3.06x adjusted EBITDA, guided below 3.0x in H2 2026.
- OE/share history (financials_history.csv): FY2023 $8.11, FY2024 $6.97, FY2025 $12.85 — the 3-yr median is $8.11.

**Base used = the engine's normalized base: median of last 3 FY OE/share = $8.11** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). Both alternatives are distorted, in opposite directions:
- Latest FY ($12.85) is distorted UP: FY2025 OCF of $990.8M includes an outsized H1 print (Q2 2025 OCF alone was $523.2M per fundamentals.json quarterly) and a $215.8M working-capital release; revenue actually fell −1.65% in FY2025.
- TTM through Q2 2026 (ttm.py, filing-direct) is distorted DOWN: OCF FY $990,800,000 − prior YTD $625,500,000 + current YTD $191,600,000 = **TTM OCF $556,900,000**; capex FY $97,700,000 − prior YTD $47,000,000 + current YTD $39,900,000 = **TTM capex $90,600,000**; SBC FY $37,300,000 − prior YTD $19,800,000 + current YTD $10,400,000 = **TTM SBC $27,900,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) **66,800,000**; **TTM OE total $438,400,000 → $6.56/share**. H1 2026 OCF collapsed (Q1 2026 OCF only $14.9M) because the company is building working capital to support AMC growth — management cut FY2026 cash-flow guidance to ~$600M for exactly that reason. A ~$600M free-cash-flow year less SBC lands near the $8.11 median, and the FY2024/FY2025 maintenance OE figures ($593.5M / $552.1M, financials_history.csv) cluster in the same zone. The median is the least-distorted of the three; the TTM figure is quoted here and used as the bear-side anchor in the verdict, not as the base.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate, installed-base not pricing-power
Justification: A real installed-base/aftermarket moat in powertrain components where downtime costs dwarf component price, but no essential IP, PES is close to commodity motors, and a decade of deal-making has produced ROIC persistently below the cost of capital — the measured history does not support a higher score.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json, annual): ROIC proxy ran 7.2% (FY2021), 3.6% (FY2022), 7.2% (FY2022 on the Dec year-end basis), 2.5% (FY2023), 4.5% (FY2024), 4.9% (FY2025) — never sustainably above a plausible cost of capital, and the Altra deal's stated aim of raising ROIC has not yet shown up in the series. Gross margin is the bright spot: 27.7% (FY2021) → 29.2% → 32.0% → 33.1% (FY2023) → 36.3% (FY2024) → 37.4% (FY2025), TTM 37.75% — real mix improvement from exiting low-margin motors and adding Altra's precision portfolio, plus pricing. Margin up, returns on the enlarged capital base still low: that is a portfolio still digesting $4.95B of acquired goodwill/intangibles, not a wide moat.
- FOR: Installed base of mission-critical components (gearboxes, couplings, bearings, brakes) where failure cost >> part cost, so spec-in positions and aftermarket demand are sticky; breadth — the ability to sell a complete powertrain/motion subsystem (cross-sell across the Rexnord + Altra portfolios) rather than a part; application engineering, distribution and service network built over decades; AMC precision brands (Kollmorgen, Portescap, Thomson) with genuine design-in positions in medical, robotics, aerospace & defense and data-center power.
- AGAINST: The company itself discloses no individual patent or group of patents is essential to the business — the moat is execution and installed base, not protected IP; PES motors/fans compete on price against global giants (ABB, Siemens) and ride weak residential HVAC/pool demand (PES organic sales −6.6% in Q2 2026); giants with deeper pockets contest every segment (Rockwell/Emerson in automation, Timken/SKF in bearings/powertrain); ROIC of 2.5–4.9% over FY2023–25 proves pricing power has not converted to capital returns through this cycle; leverage (net debt 7.9x normalized OE) leaves no room for a bad cycle.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth recalibration (written reason):** the engine's blended start of 10.12% is an acquisition artifact and fails the sanity check against actual prints. Its components: 5-yr revenue CAGR 15.36% (straddles the 2021 Rexnord merger and the 2023 Altra deal — revenue went $3.81B → $5.22B → $6.25B by acquisition, not organically), 3-yr revenue CAGR 4.38%, latest FY revenue YoY −1.65%, OE/share CAGR 2y 25.82% (off the distorted FY2023/FY2025 bases above). Actual current prints: FY2025 revenue −1.6%, Q2 2026 sales +4.2% reported / +3.3% organic, orders +8.8% daily, and 2026 guidance of $6.2B revenue (≈ +4.5% vs FY2025) with adjusted EPS midpoint held at $10.60. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.1212 / −0.0912 / −0.0612 / −0.0312 / +0.0088 vs g_base) to −2 / 1 / **4** / 7 / 11%. Probabilities kept at the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults; OE multipliers at the 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 defaults — the evidence (strong AMC orders vs weak PES, high leverage, CEO transition) argues for spread, not skew. Price $154.01.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −2.0% | 0.75 | Industrial recession; PES/HVAC slump spreads; WC build eats cash; deleveraging stalls | $41.93 | 5.78% |
| Bear | 25% | 1.0% | 0.90 | TTM-like cash conversion persists (~$6.56/sh zone); low-single-digit organic growth | $56.52 | 7.04% |
| Base | 30% | 4.0% | 1.00 | Guidance-like path: ~$6.2B revenue, AMC data-center/automation strength offsets PES | $70.49 | 8.27% |
| Bull | 25% | 7.0% | 1.10 | Orders (+8.8%) convert; ePOD ramps 2027+; synergies lift cash conversion toward FY2025 quality | $86.94 | 9.68% |
| Super bull | 10% | 11.0% | 1.25 | Full Altra thesis lands: subsystem cross-sell, ROIC finally inflects, sustained high-single-digit organic growth | $114.90 | 11.99% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $72.69 (−52.8% vs price), IV@12% $96.16, IV@10% $122.28, weighted IRR 8.47%, base-case IRR 8.27%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D at 7.04%, bull D at 9.68% — the band no longer spans tiers after recalibration). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 5.27%, terminal value 18.3% of IV@15%, scenario spread 2.74x, net debt 7.90x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (dcf_numbers.json): the $154.01 price clears 15% only at $72.69 — i.e., the stock would need to fall ~53% for the weighted case to clear Andrew's 15% hurdle; it clears 20% at $51.53 and 25% at $39.83.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended ~10 months ago): resolved by inspection, not by switching base — ttm.py was run and its legs are quoted in full above (TTM OE $438,400,000 = $6.56/share through Q2 2026). The TTM base was rejected as the primary base because H1 2026 OCF is depressed by a deliberate AMC working-capital build (Q1 2026 OCF $14.9M; FY cash-flow guidance cut to ~$600M for that build); the 3-yr median base is retained and the TTM figure anchors the bear case. The final run therefore does not pass --ttm.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (NI vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): explained, and it is structural deal accounting plus working capital, not hidden earnings quality fraud. FY2023: net income −$57.4M vs OCF $715.3M — D&A was $492.8M that year (financials_history.csv; Altra close-year amortization/impairment-scale charges vs $165.3M in FY2024 and $154.5M in FY2025) plus heavy interest on the acquisition debt crushed reported NI while cash flow held. FY2024: NI $196.2M vs OCF $609.4M — D&A $165.3M plus a $341.5M working-capital release. FY2025: NI $279.5M vs OCF $990.8M — D&A $154.5M plus a $215.8M working-capital release. The OCF-based conservative OE is the series used throughout, but the same WC releases that explain the divergence are why the FY2025 OE print is not trusted as the base (see next flag).
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $12.85 vs 3-yr median $8.11): the LATEST year is the distorted one. FY2025 OCF was inflated by the H1/Q2 2025 spike (Q2 2025 OCF $523.2M, fundamentals.json quarterly) and the $215.8M WC release, on revenue that fell −1.65%. The median ($8.11) is corroborated by maintenance OE (FY2024 $593.5M, FY2025 $552.1M) and by 2026 cash-flow guidance ~$600M. Median retained as base; latest and TTM ($6.56) bracket it from above and below.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 7.9x normalized OE): confirmed from the filing basis — net debt $4,267,000,000 (LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent, less cash $521,700,000 on the FY2025 history line), plus $152,500,000 of lease liabilities. This is Altra-deal debt being paid down (debt total was $6,380,900,000 at FY2023-end). On the company's own adjusted-EBITDA yardstick leverage was 3.06x at Q2 2026, guided below 3.0x in H2 2026 — manageable if cash conversion recovers, dangerous if the TTM $6.56/sh cash generation is the new normal: at TTM OE the same net debt is ~9.7x by simple division of the two quoted figures' relationship (stated in words, not used as a model input). Bear cases were stressed via the 0.75/0.90 OE multipliers.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.5x in the preliminary run): was an artifact of the un-recalibrated 10.12% blend start and the default ±12pp offsets; after the written recalibration above the spread is 2.74x. Confidence is still capped at medium (never high with this leverage and base uncertainty).
- **TIER_BAND** (preliminary run: bear D 8.0% vs bull C 12.7%): resolved by the same recalibration — in the final run bear (7.04%), base (8.27%) and bull (9.68%) are all Tier D, so there is no cross-tier band left to size against; the verdict is sized to the whole D band regardless.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, and unusually all three candidate bases tell the same verdict story at $154.01: on the median base the weighted IRR is 8.47% (Tier D); the preliminary engine run (median base, un-recalibrated 10.12% growth) printed 10.71% (Tier C) — that C is bought entirely with acquisition-inflated growth; on the TTM base ($6.56/sh) the result would be lower still. No defensible method gets this price near the 15% hurdle — the hurdle price on the final run is $72.69.
- What the market is paying for is visible in Q2 2026: orders +8.8%, AMC orders +17.1% with data-center strength, adjusted EPS $2.99 (including a $0.39 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit — a one-off; $48M / $0.57 per share of refunds is baked into 2026 guidance), gross margin still expanding, and an ePOD data-center ramp mostly in 2027+. Some of that is real. But adjusted EPS of $10.60 guided for 2026 sits far above GAAP EPS guidance of $5.42–$5.92 — the gap is the amortization/restructuring the OE method refuses to wave away, and cash conversion (TTM OE $6.56/sh) currently agrees with GAAP, not with adjusted.
- Quality check: SBC is genuinely small ($27.9M TTM, <1% of revenue) — no dilution games; share count is flat (66.6M → 66.8M diluted). The problem is not the income statement's honesty, it is the balance sheet and the price: $4.27B of net debt against $438–856M of OE depending on the year's WC weather, and a $10.26B market cap that needs the super-bull decade to clear even ~12%.
- What would change the verdict: two or three quarters of TTM OE recovering toward $8+/share as the AMC working capital converts to shipments, net debt/adjusted EBITDA through 2.5x, and ROIC printing above ~7% — evidence the Altra capital is finally earning its keep. Until then the deleveraging story is a bondholder's thesis, not an equity compounder at this price.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.47% on the final inputs; defensible method range D–C, with the C requiring the acquisition-inflated growth blend this analysis rejects in writing)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing arithmetic and the base triangulation; the scenario spread is 2.74x and leverage makes the bear case genuinely bad, so no higher)
- One-liner: Levered industrial roll-up, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $154.01 (weighted IRR 8.5%, IV@15% $72.69); it would need to fall to ~$73 to clear the hurdle on the normalized $8.11/share base.
